title: The Almost Tryouts
premise: Juniper Ravensworth has spent two years at Ashgrove Academy being invisible, until a recipe card in his late grandmother's box turns out to be a coded ledger implicating the school board in funneling scholarship students into an off-books 'enrichment program' that quietly funnels their tuition trust into board members' pockets. As Juniper decodes the rest of the cards, he discovers his grandmother was a whistleblower who died before she could publish, and that the board's enforcer, Dean Corliss-Hale, already knows someone is reading them. With the help of three fellow 'almosts'—students who nearly got scholarships and know how the system grinds—Juniper must reconstruct the full paper trail and expose it at the Founders' Gala. The book ends with the board dissolved mid-gala as the evidence airs publicly; Juniper keeps his grandmother's name attached to the exposé, finally belonging somewhere on purpose.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is a former boarding-school scholarship kid from coastal Maine who writes about institutions with too many locked doors. He lives with a rescue greyhound and a suspiciously organized spice rack.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Establishes Ashgrove's invisible caste system: scholarship kids eat last, speak softly, and never open their lockers near faculty. Juniper's careful routine cracks when a janitor warns him someone's been asking about his family name. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Back home for fall break, Juniper inherits grandma Maren's recipe box and finds cards written in cipher between the gingerbread and the pickles—one card lists student names and dollar amounts. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Almosts
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Back at school, Juniper cautiously recruits Odile (waitlisted twice), Theo (kicked out when his funding 'lapsed'), and Priya (student archivist). They confirm one listed student vanished mid-semester last year. Emotional beat: first fragile trust.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: POV Priya. In the archives, Priya finds the 'Enrichment Trust'—a fund meant for scholarship students, drained annually since 1998. A photo shows young Dean Corliss-Hale beside Maren Ravensworth. Emotional beat: the past feeling suddenly personal.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Someone searches Juniper's locker and leaves a printed copy of one decoded card—a warning. Corliss-Hale offers him a 'legacy enrichment stipend' if he returns what he found. Emotional beat: fear wearing the mask of generosity.

chapters.title: Cipher Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The four decode more cards in the night kitchen, learning Maren was the trust's original auditor and that her 'accident' came weeks after her final report. Theo confesses his expulsion was retaliation for asking where the money went. Emotional beat: rage becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Vanished Girl
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Tracking the missing student, Lena Okafor, they find she didn't vanish—she transferred under pressure after discovering the scheme, and she'll talk, but only in person. Odile risks expulsion sneaking off-campus to reach her. Emotional beat: courage without a safety net.

chapters.title: Corliss-Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Lena hands over corroborating records, but Corliss-Hale intercepts Juniper, reveals he knows about Maren, and threatens every Almost's future. Juniper realizes the gala in six days is the only moment all trustees will be in one room. Emotional beat: cornered, then clear-eyed.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV rotating among all four. A montage of preparation: copying archives, coaching Lena's testimony, planting USB drives, and a near-betrayal when Theo wavers under a reinstatement offer. Emotional beat: the cost of the plan counted honestly.

chapters.title: Founders' Gala
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. During the toast, the lights fail and the evidence runs across every screen: ledgers, signatures, Maren's final audit, Lena's voice. Trustees scatter; Corliss-Hale is escorted out mid-denial. Juniper credits 'Maren Ravensworth, auditor' aloud—and the Almosts stand together, seen. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, belonging inside it.
